title: Comprehensive Kannada Basics Practice
description: Practice day-to-day Kannada using multiple question types.

questions.explanation: Use 'beku' after the object you want.
Use 'ista illa' to express don't like.
Use 'beku' after the thing you want.
'Hogta idini' is present continuous 'I am going'.
'Barta idini' is present continuous 'I am coming'.
'Maadta idini' is present continuous 'I am doing'.
'Tinnuta idini' is present continuous 'I am eating'.
'Kudita idini' is present continuous 'I am drinking'.
'Ooduta idini' is present continuous 'I am reading'.
'Keluta idini' is present continuous 'I am listening'.
'Noduta idini' is present continuous 'I am watching'.
Essential expressions for wants and likes.
Past and future forms for various verbs.
Adjectives from the notes (some like 'sogadu' for taste).
Question words used in day-to-day conversations.
'Beda' means don't want, so this means 'I don't want water.'
'Tinnide' is past tense; it means 'I ate.'

questions.statement: 'Naanu oota tinnuta idini' means 'I am eating.'

questions.explanation: 'Kelage' means down/below; 'melage' would be up (not in notes).
'Alli' means in or at a location.
'Banni' is used as a polite/plural imperative.
Correct: 'Kodi' is used politely to ask someone to give.
'Hogutini' is future; it means 'I will go'.
'Barta idini' is present continuous 'I am coming'.
'Tinnuta idini' is present continuous 'I am eating'.
'Beku' means want / need; 'bekku' is cat (not in notes).

questions.situation: You are at a restaurant and want to politely ask for water.
questions.explanation: 'Nannage neeru kodi' means 'Please give me water'.

questions.situation: You are offered coffee but you don't want it.
You're calling your friend inside your house informally.
You're talking to a shopkeeper politely and want them to come here.
questions.explanation: 'Banni illi' politely asks someone to come here.

questions.situation: You need someone to listen carefully.
You want to tell an auto driver politely to go to MG Road.
questions.explanation: 'Hogi sir' politely tells them to go.

questions.situation: You're at a friend's place and want to politely ask them to give you the book.
You want to tell a child to eat food.
questions.explanation: 'Oota tinnu' is an informal command to eat.

questions.situation: You want to tell an elder to eat food politely.
You want to ask someone politely to read the book.
You're at your office; you want to tell your colleague politely to come out.
You want to tell a friend: I am going to the market.
questions.explanation: Present continuous form suits 'I am going'.

questions.situation: You want to tell a friend: I will go to the office.
You need to ask politely if someone likes coffee.
You want to ask politely if someone likes tea.
questions.explanation: Use 'ista?' to ask if they like something.

questions.situation: You want to ask politely if someone wants water.
You're telling someone politely that you don't want water.
questions.explanation: 'Nannage neeru beda' means 'I don't want water'.
